title: If You Missed 2.5% Mortgages... It's Happening Again
creator: MarketBeat
summary: MarketBeat host Bridget interviews Ronan McMahon of Real Estate Trend Alert on international property as an alternative to US real estate, where rising mortgage rates have cooled home sales. McMahon, who holds 80-90% of his net worth in property across nine countries, argues the best opportunities are in places at the early stages of multi-decade transformations, and recommends an 8-year minimum horizon. His three picks: Panama City, Panama (number three) — a global hub city where luxury condos from $400 per square foot can be rented long-term to executives at firms like Pfizer and Ernst & Young for double-digit yields, though short-term renting is restricted and developer finance (not bank mortgages) is the route in; Guanacaste, Costa Rica (number two) — centred on Tamarindo, accessible via the expanded Liberia airport, with $400-500K condos for the affluent international market, but dollar borrowing at roughly US rates; and Lagos, Portugal (number one) — an Algarve beach, marina and historic old town where foreigners can borrow at 2.5-2.6%, earn 12-16% gross (7-8% net) short-term rental yields, and target doubling invested capital every five years. A bonus lifestyle pick is Sicily, where renovated homes in good towns run $50-100K. No stock tickers, REITs or ETFs are mentioned and no stock calls are made. The episode also promotes McMahon's free book, The Big Book of Profitable Real Estate Investing.
